scope: Proposition 7.5 (Haar block information bound) of the manuscript “Posterior replicas and conditional information in Gaussian regression” (preprints/Posterior-replicas-and-conditional-information-in-Gaussian-regression-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 140 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 135be898557ce66e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 36. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let S ∼ σ, let V be a finite-valued state, and let a block consist of k = ⌊d/16⌋ fresh independent standard Gaussian designs, independent of (S, V ) and the past, with their exact labels. Suppose a finite-valued state W is generated by a measurable randomized kernel from V and the full block, with no other retained information from the past. Let B be a Haar ℓ = ⌊d/4⌋ frame drawn independently of the entire joint experiment producing S, V , the block, and W. Then I(S; W | V, B, BS) ≤ H(W | V ) m + Cd + log(1 + Cd + H(V )) + C H(V ) + log d d2 , m = ⌊d/16⌋ + 1. (97) The constant C is absolute. If every state has logarithmic width at most H∗ = o(d2), the left side is at most Cd for all sufficiently large d.
